EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  MAY 29, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:05 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Patricia Harik
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 23, 2018
MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE APRIL 23, 2018 ADJOURNED
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
A letter from Kathy Chessmore, 37 Empty Saddle Lane, regarding her concerns about the
California Water Service Company water reliability project was reviewed.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE
WRITEN COMMUNICATION.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korina Winji and John Collazo from California Water Service Company distributed and
reviewed a pamphlet being provided to horse owners potentially impacted by the Water
Reliability Project along the City’s bridle trails where new water pipes will be installed as early
as mid-July 2018.  Patty Humphrey, 14 Pony Lane, had several questions for the California
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 29, 2018  1
 Water Service Company representatives, including “Can I start boarding now, since a stall is
available?” and indicated her concerns that the communications were lacking from this
company, boarders on Phillips Canyon Trail would be landlocked during the project, and
recommended a website be set up by California Water Service for equestrians to receive up-
to-date information.

In response to an inquiries from CHAIRMAN MITCHELL, Ms. Winji stated that impacted horse
owners would be receiving $800/month per horse up front in two lump sum payments if
required to be relocated during the project. She clarified that these payments were for
incremental fees, not boarding fees that they would normally pay. She also responded that
20 to 25 horses may need to be relocated due to the project. In addition, Ms. Winji clarified
that there would be temporary metal plates covering any street trenches, but would not likely
be in place for more than 48 hours, in response to a concern about horse owners in the Larga
Vista HOA who may want to cross at Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East.
She stated that she would reach out and notify all of the horse owners in that neighborhood.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL inquired whether the use of Ernie Howlett Park’s barn should be
considered again, since horse owners needed to be temporarily relocated felt that the PV
Stables was much too far from the east side of Rolling Hills Estates. Several Committee
Members noted that the Howlett Park barn stall would all be needed for all the horse shows
and that the park is locked at dusk, which would not meet the needs of the relocated horse
owners. Becky Martin, LSAC Horse Show Chair, stated that they need all of the inside stalls
for their shows. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL then suggested that the Fitzpatrick boarding facility
below Ernie Howlett Park be allowed to expand their boarding units temporarily, but
Committee Members indicated that the additional stalls they once had on this site had been
removed. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL asked Ms. Winji to provide the City a copy of the draft
Boarding Agreement that California Water Service is developing.

MEMBER SHINN suggested that the project be delayed to allow Gil Houle to have the
temporary pipe corrals built. She also recommended that the construction workers have a
short training in horse behavior. Audience Member, Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road,
recommended that equestrians always walk their horse when near construction sites.
MEMBER SILVANO reminded the California Water Representatives that when a horse owner
moves a horse into stall owned by a resident, that typically the horse owner incurs additional
costs to make improvements to the stall before moving their horse into the stall. MEMBER
PERSICHINA recommended placement of street signs forewarning drivers of the upcoming
road closure. Mr. Callazo responded that they have been working on this for several months
with all of the Cities surrounding Rolling Hills Estates. He also agreed with Committee
Members that all of the trail warning signs should be installed by the end of June 2018.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET
The Community Services Director reviewed the draft Trail Safety Pamphlet and requested
comments and suggestions for its improvement. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL noted that the “no
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 29, 2018  2
 wheeled vehicles on trails” ordinance had been left off this draft. MEMBER SILVANO noted
that there was a typo on City Hall’s street address. The Community Services Director
thanked the Committee for all their input to making a good trail safety pamphlet and that the
corrections noted at this meeting would be made before distributing them.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CITY CELEBRATION VENUE UPDATE
The Community Services Director reported that the City Celebration Subcommittee planning
the Schedule of Events at the Empty Saddle Club venue had met that evening and the focus
would be on the equestrian activities this year.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CHANDLER PARK TEMPORARY VIDEO CAMERA UPDATE
The Community Services Director shared Chandler Park arena usage statistics thus far.
Richard Oldroyd, 40 Ranchview Road, thanked staff for responding to his questions about the
future installation of video cameras in City parks.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

MAYORS BREAKFAST RIDE UPDATE

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL thanked everyone for making this Mayor’s Ride the most successful
in decades.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported on a recent meeting with Jessica Slawson, who was still in training
for her position that includes the City’s emergency response planning. She also reported that
there will be an upcoming horse chipping clinic, a trailering clinic, hosting the ERT Level 1
course at City Hall, and development of evacuation plans for the City’s equestrians.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 29, 2018  3
 HIGH SCHOOL EQUESTRIAN TEAM
Sean Martin, 2 Empty Saddle Road, stated that the Peninsula High School had cancelled the
school’s Equestrian Team program with short notice and incorrect information due to a
recommendation from the District’s legal department. A number of parents and students
addressed the Committee requesting support from the City to have a letter of concern sent to
the School District for the June 20, 2018 School Board meeting.

MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO RECOMMEND THAT CITY COUNCIL SEND A LETTER OF CONCERN
  REGARDING THE CANCELLATION OF PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HIGH
  SCHOOL’S EQUESTRIAN TEAM PROGRAM.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

CHANDLER PARK ARENA SUMMER RECREATIONAL RIDING PERIODS
The Community Services Director indicated that the new recreational riding periods approved
by the Committee would go into effect on June 1 st. Pam Schachter, 40 Ranchview Road,
requested and received an exception to the new periods on a once-per-month basis.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER HARIK reported that brush clearing was needed near the Rolling Hills Little
  League field trails area.

  The Community Services Director requested and received approval from the
  Committee to move the July 23rd Equestrian Committee Meeting to July 30th.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
MAY 29, 2018  4
 C.  CITY CELEBRATION VENUE UPDATE – June 25, 2018

D.  SCHOOL BOARD MEETING UPDATE – June 25, 2018

E.  CHANDLER PARK VIDEO SURVEILLANCE UPDATE – June 25, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 9:01 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
